show_title: Invest Like the Best with Patrick O'Shaughnessy
title: Arianna Simpson – The Crypto Landscape - [Invest Like the Best, EP.84]
thesis: This episode argues that the crypto landscape is still in a phase of figuring out long-term token economics and which specific strategies will work, with a focus on the 'fat protocol' thesis. The speaker maintains a neutral stance, noting that while Bitcoin has a blue chip aura, its privacy and throughput are concerns, and Ethereum fits the fat protocol story but remains uncertain.

claims.claim: The speaker notes that R chain uses a concurrent model to process transactions in multiple lanes simultaneously, but admits uncertainty about which strategies will work long-term.
claims.quote: But if you look at something like R chain, for example, they are using a concurrent model whereby you can process transactions concurrently unless they're directly related to a transaction that happened previously.

claims.claim: The speaker mentions that Ethereum plays nicely into the fat protocol thesis story, but notes that long-term token economics are still being figured out.
claims.quote: You look at something like Ethereum that plays very nicely into that story. We'll see. I think a lot of the long-term token economics are still being figured out.

claims.claim: The speaker states they are not a Bitcoin maximalist, acknowledging Bitcoin has a blue chip aura but noting its privacy is not great and transaction throughput could be problematic if everything settles back into it.
claims.quote: So I'm not a Bitcoin maximalist in the sense that, you know, I don't think everything is going back to that. But I do think that at this point, it has kind of this blue chip aura and, which is funny, because I very much remember the days where I was like, oh, it's only used for drugs, um, which clearly isn't the case.

claims.claim: The speaker compares Monero to Zcash, suggesting Monero is potentially more at risk from regulatory scrutiny due to its non-traditional company structure relative to Zcash.
claims.quote: So, for example, I think, yes, privacy coins are, as a general category, probably more likely to be closely watched, if not worse, from regulatory authorities. And even within that, you know, I think something like Monero is potentially more at risk because they have a non-traditional company structure and that sort of thing, relative to, let's say, Z-cash.
